CRITICAL RULES (violating these fails the whole benchmark):
- You may ONLY learn about /workspace/executable by RUNNING it with different arguments/stdin/env.
- You MUST NOT use objdump, nm, strings, gdb, ghidra, strace, ltrace, readelf, or any disassembler/tracer on /workspace/executable.
- You MUST NOT search the web or any package registry for the source code of this project.
- Do not modify /workspace/executable. Work in /tmp.
The binary is a clone of the 'cat' utility with syntax highlighting (it self-identifies as "bat 0.26.1").
Docs available to read: /workspace/README.md, /workspace/doc/short-help.txt, /workspace/doc/long-help.txt.

NOTE: the ambient environment has NO_COLOR=1 and TERM=dumb set. When probing, control this explicitly
(e.g. 'env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm-256color /workspace/executable ...') and RECORD which env you used.
Always pipe output through 'cat -A' or 'od -c' when whitespace/escapes matter, and record exit codes.

Map how /workspace/executable behaves with respect to environment variables and TTY detection.
Environment variables to test: NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, FORCE_COLOR, TERM (dumb, xterm,
xterm-256color, unset), COLORTERM (truecolor, 24bit), COLUMNS, BAT_WIDTH, BAT_STYLE, BAT_THEME,
BAT_THEME_DARK, BAT_THEME_LIGHT, BAT_TABS, BAT_PAGER, PAGER, BAT_PAGING, BAT_OPTS, BAT_CONFIG_PATH,
BAT_CONFIG_DIR, BAT_CACHE_PATH, LESS, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, HOME.
For each: what changes? Precedence vs CLI flags. Exact values accepted (e.g. is NO_COLOR= empty treated as unset?).
TTY behavior: use 'script -qec "..." /dev/null' to simulate a TTY and determine what changes when stdout is a
terminal: default --color, default --decorations, default --paging, default --style ('auto'), terminal width
detection, whether the theme auto-detection queries the terminal (does it emit an escape sequence like
'\x1b]11;?\x07' to ask for the background color? check with a pty capture).
Does bat check if STDIN is a TTY (for the no-arguments case)? What does it do with no args on a TTY?
Also: does truecolor output (24-bit '38;2;R;G;B') get used when COLORTERM=truecolor, instead of 256-color?
This is IMPORTANT - test '--color=always' with COLORTERM=truecolor vs unset for the same file and record
both escape sequences.
Write your full detailed findings to /tmp/spec/12-env-tty.md. Be exhaustive and concrete:
include exact literal output text (byte-for-byte, with escapes spelled out), exact error message strings,
exit codes, and the precise command lines that produce them. Someone must be able to reimplement the
behavior from your file WITHOUT running the binary again. Do not summarize away details.
Your returned text should be a short (<=25 line) summary of the most important findings only.

6 7 ## Key Features 8 9 ### Syntax highlighting 10 11 `bat` supports syntax highlighting for a large number of programming and markup languages. 12 13 ### Git integration 14 15 `bat` communicates with `git` to show modifications with respect to the index. 16 17 ### Show non-printable characters 18 19 You can use the `-A`/`--show-all` option to show and highlight non-printable characters. 20 21 ### Automatic paging 22 23 By default, `bat` pipes its own output to a pager (e.g. `less`) if the output is too large for one screen. 24 If you would rather `bat` work like `cat` all the time (never page output), you can set `--paging=never` as an option, either on the command line or in your configuration file. 25 If you intend to alias `cat` to `bat` in your shell configuration, you can use `alias cat='bat --paging=never'` to preserve the default behavior. 26 27 #### File concatenation 28 29 Even with a pager set, you can still use `bat` to concatenate files. 30 Whenever `bat` detects a non-interactive terminal (i.e. when you pipe into another process or into a file), `bat` will act as a drop-in replacement for `cat` and fall back to printing the plain file contents, regardless of the `--pager` option's value. 31 32 ## How to use 33 34 Display a single file on the terminal: 35 36 ```bash 37 bat README.md 38 ``` 39 40 Display multiple files at once: 41 42 ```bash 43 bat src/*.rs 44 ``` 45 46 Read from stdin, determine the syntax automatically: 47 48 ```bash 49 curl -s https://sh.rustup.rs | bat 50 ``` 51 52 Read from stdin, specify the language explicitly: 53 54 ```bash 55 yaml2json .travis.yml | json_pp | bat -l json 56 ``` 57 58 Show and highlight non-printable characters: 59 60 ```bash 61 bat -A /etc/hosts 62 ``` 63 64 Use it as a `cat` replacement: 65 66 ```bash 67 bat > note.md # quickly create a new file 68 69 bat header.md content.md footer.md > document.md 70 71 bat -n main.rs # show line numbers (only) 72 73 bat f - g # output 'f', then stdin, then 'g'. 74 ``` 75 76 ### Integration with other tools 77 78 #### `fzf` 79 80 You can use `bat` as a previewer for `fzf`: 81 82 ```bash 83 fzf --preview "bat --color=always --style=numbers --line-range=:500 {}" 84 ``` 85 86 #### `find` or `fd` 87 88 Preview all search results with `bat`: 89 90 ```bash 91 find … -exec bat {} + 92 fd … -X bat 93 ``` 94 95 #### `ripgrep` 96 97 With `batgrep`, `bat` can be used as the printer for `ripgrep` search results: 98 99 ```bash 100 batgrep needle src/ 101 ``` 102 103 #### `tail -f` 104 105 `bat` can be combined with `tail -f` to continuously monitor a given file with syntax highlighting: 106 107 ```bash 108 tail -f /var/log/pacman.log | bat --paging=never -l log 109 ``` 110 111 #### `git` 112 113 Combine `bat` with `git show` to view an older version of a file with syntax highlighting: 114 115 ```bash 116 git show v0.6.0:src/main.rs | bat -l rs 117 ``` 118 119 #### `git diff` 120 121 Combine `bat` with `git diff` to view lines around code changes: 122 123 ```bash 124 batdiff() { 125 git diff --name-only --relative --diff-filter=d -z | xargs -0 bat --diff 126 } 127 ``` 128 129 #### `xclip` 130 131 Pipe the output into `xclip` to copy file contents: 132 133 ```bash 134 bat main.cpp | xclip 135 ``` 136 137 `bat` will detect that the output is being redirected and print the plain file contents. 138 139 #### `man` 140 141 `bat` can be used as a colorizing pager for `man`: 142 143 ```bash 144 export MANPAGER="bat -plman" 145 man 2 select 146 ``` 147 148 #### Highlighting `--help` messages 149 150 You can use `bat` to colorize help text: 151 152 ```bash 153 cp --help | bat -plhelp 154 ``` 155 156 Or use a wrapper: 157 158 ```bash 159 alias bathelp='bat --plain --language=help' 160 help() { 161 "$@" --help 2>&1 | bathelp 162 } 163 ``` 164 165 ## Installation 166 167 Download prebuilt binaries from the release page for your platform. 168 169 `bat` is also available through various package managers: 170 171 - ap.add_argument("--stdin-pipe", default=None, help="feed this data via a pipe on stdin instead of pty")
ap.add_argument("--stdout-pipe", action="store_true", help="stdout is a pipe, stdin is the pty")
ap.add_argument("cmd", nargs="+")
a = ap.parse_args()

env = {}
for e in a.env:
    if "=" in e:
        k, v = e.split("=", 1); env[k] = v
    else:
        env.pop(e, None)

pid, fd = pty.fork()
if pid == 0:
    # child
    if a.stdin_pipe is not None:
        r, w = os.pipe()
        os.write(w, a.stdin_pipe.encode().decode("unicode_escape").encode("latin1"))
        os.close(w)
        os.dup2(r, 0)
    if a.stdout_pipe:
        # replace stdout with a pipe to a file
        f = os.open("/tmp/probe/child_stdout.bin", os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_TRUNC)
        os.dup2(f, 1)
    try:
        os.execve(a.cmd[0], a.cmd, env)
    except Exception as ex:
        os.write(2, str(ex).encode())
        os._exit(127)

fcntl.ioctl(fd, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, struct.pack("HHHH", a.rows, a.cols, 0, 0))
buf = b""
replied = False
start = time.time()
reply = a.reply.encode().decode("unicode_escape").encode("latin1") if a.reply else None
while True:
    if time.time() - start > a.timeout:
        break
    try:
        r, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.2)
    except OSError:
        break
    if fd in r:
        try:
            d = os.read(fd, 65536)
        except OSError:
            break
        if not d:
            break
        buf += d
        if reply and not replied and (b"\x1b]11;?" in buf or b"\x1b]10;?" in buf):
            replied = True
            os.write(fd, reply)
    else:
        # check if child exited
        p, st = os.waitpid(pid, os.WNOHANG)
        if p == pid:
            # drain
            while True:
                try:
                    rr, _, _ = select.select([fd], [], [], 0.1)
                    if fd not in rr: break
                    d = os.read(fd, 65536)
                    if not d: break
                    buf += d
                except OSError:
                    break
            break

    p, st = os.waitpid(pid, 0)
    code = os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(st)
except ChildProcessError:
    code = None
except Exception:
    code = None
open(a.out, "wb").write(buf)
sys.stderr.write("EXITCODE=%s BYTES=%d\n" % (code, len(buf)))
EOF
echo ok
